question.text: The number of solutions of equation $(4-\sqrt{3}) \sin x$ $-2 \sqrt{3} \cos ^2 x=-\frac{4}{1+\sqrt{3}}, x \in\left[-2 \pi, \frac{5 \pi}{2}\right]$ is

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & (4-\sqrt{3}) \sin x-2 \sqrt{3} \cos ^2 x=\frac{-4}{1+\sqrt{3}}, x \in\left[-2 \pi, \frac{5 \pi}{2}\right] \\ & \Rightarrow(4-\sqrt{3}) \sin x-2 \sqrt{3}\left(1-\sin ^2 x\right)=2(1-\sqrt{3}) \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \sqrt{3} \sin ^2 x+4 \sin x-\sqrt{3} \sin x-2=0 \\ & \Rightarrow(2 \sin x-1)(\sqrt{3} \sin x+2)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \sin x=\frac{1}{2} \\ & \therefore \text { Number of solution }=5\end{aligned}$
